title: Native Uint64 Bitwise V1
objective: Implement generic source-transparent typed uint64 bitwise and shift operators in IR, dynamic fallback, native C lowering, explain/inspect output, and differential property tests with defined shift semantics
scope_notes: The lane expanded from native-compiler to compiler-runtime after the frontend revealed that Sage mode normalized CPython xor to exponentiation even under the existing explicit native-bitwise marker. The only frontend change preserves `^` and `^=` under that marker and leaves ordinary Sage exponentiation unchanged.

handoff.summary: Implemented canonical typed uint64 &, |, ^, <<, and >> operations across exact, binary64, and source-transparent prime IR plus portable JavaScript, isolated C, word, tagged, and prime-source backends. Added augmented scalar and UInt64Buffer lowering with Python target-before-RHS evaluation order, explicit 0..63 shift guards, logical right shift, modulo-2^64 left shift, Sage-mode xor marker preservation, IR v22, cache fingerprinting, explain metadata, focused differential/property coverage, benchmark coverage, compiler documentation, and Node test-manifest registration.
risks: The broad compiler tier failed outside this claim: compiler/algebra.py timed out and compiler/matrix.py hit an existing sparse-random runtime error under Node 26.7.0.
The broad integration tier passed 371/380 tests but failed eight matrix/polynomial runtime tests outside this claim; focused native-kernel, FFI, build, architecture, and strict checks pass.

CPython's annotation-only uint64 fallback retains Python int left-shift behavior; full-word wrapping and 0..63 guards are the documented typed-IR/native/portable-JavaScript contract, so cross-path source that can overflow must mask explicitly.
next_steps: Integration lane: in src/lib/sagejs/native.py, change the module docstring's `Native Kernel v21` to `Native Kernel v22` and add the documented typed uint64 contract: &, |, and ^ operate on the full unsigned word; left shift wraps modulo 2^64; right shift is logical; compiled/typed-JavaScript shift counts are 0..63 with OverflowError for 64+, negative values fail the uint64 boundary, `# sagejs: native-bitwise` preserves ^ as xor in Sage mode, and CPython's annotation-only fallback retains int shift behavior.

Integration lane: rerun pnpm test:compiler and pnpm test:integration after rebasing onto the current integration base and preparing its native cache; investigate only if the recorded unrelated matrix/polynomial failures remain.
The test manifest follow-up is already complete in this lane: test/native-uint64-bitwise.cjs is registered in test/node-test-manifest.cjs.
